leo martins: Hey team — planning a ~60-day work trip to Porto (2024-09-01 to 2024-10-30). Quick checklist before I book: 1) Is the WFH stipend pro-rated for a two-month temporary homebase? 2) Can corporate laptop be shipped to my short-term address (VAT/customs)? 3) Any payroll/tax nexus risk for Redwood for ~60 days? 4) If I do an in-person interview with a candidate while there, does that change anything?
maya (people-ops): Thanks Leo. Please submit the Temporary Homebase form (https://intranet.redwood/work-remote). Short answers: stipend prorated by calendar days; shipments go through our approved logistics vendor where possible; payroll/legal need to triage nexus but 60 days is low risk in most countries. For interviews: in-person recruiting can increase local risk — please flag if you expect to meet candidates.
leo martins: Form submitted + temporary address attached. I might do one coffee interview with a candidate in Lisbon area (informal). Not client-facing work, mostly product infra.
sanjay (payroll): @leo martins thanks. Payroll note: 60 days is usually below the 183-day residence threshold, but employer obligations can appear earlier if work is performed for local clients or you hire locally. Since you said internal infra and one informal interview, risk is low but we will run the nexus check. Don't change bank details until payroll confirms.
nora (legal): Adding legal view: Portugal tax residency ~183 days; however, permanent establishment and social security rules can trigger depending on activities. An informal coffee meeting is unlikely to create employer obligations but formal recruiting or signing offers locally could change that. We'll open an advisory with our tax counsel to be safe.
logistics: If you choose the "international ship" option when filling the form we will attempt vendor-managed import to reduce VAT where allowed. If vendor cannot ship, you can request a personal-ship pre-approval and expense reimbursement for customs/VAT, but that requires receipts and pre-approval. For laptops, export controls are minimal for EU shipments but stock availability may affect timing (allow 10 business days).
maya (people-ops): Also note: benefits (health, pension) generally continue while on temporary homebase, but network providers/in-country coverage varies. If you have country-specific provider questions, attach your benefits plan ID to the form and we'll check. Reminder: submit >=15 business days before travel for full checks.
leo martins: Quick follow-ups: 1) If vendor handles VAT but charges import VAT, is that reimbursed? 2) If tax counsel flags a small employer obligation, what's the likely lead time for payroll changes so I don't get surprised mid-trip?
sanjay (payroll): Typically vendor-managed import VAT is billed to corporate PO and not a personal expense. If we have to move payroll or withhold locally, payroll needs ~2 pay cycles to implement changes. We'll aim to avoid mid-trip changes but will give explicit notice.
nora (legal): We're opening the advisory ticket now. To expedite: confirm the one-line role summary while abroad (leo: "internal infra, minimal local recruiting") and whether you will sign any offer letters or invoices locally. If you might, flag immediately.
leo martins: Confirmed: internal infra, minimal local recruiting (informal coffee only), will not sign offers or invoices locally. Will wait for the advisory.
hr-bot: AUTOMATED: Temporary homebase requests must include travel dates, temporary address, and required attachments (visa/permit if applicable). Requests submitted <15 business days before travel may be processed but could be delayed. See https://intranet.redwood/forms/temp-remote
maya (people-ops): Great — next steps: legal opens advisory with tax counsel (nora), payroll runs nexus check (sanjay), logistics confirms shipping ETA. We'll update you in this thread by EOD. If you need to book housing before checks finish DM me and we can provide a provisional note but it's at your own risk until tax/payroll confirm.
leo martins: Thanks all — holding off on the reservation until I hear back. Appreciate the clarity. :thumbsup:
